MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The fender washers feel like a natural next purchase because they complement my metric bolt assortments and help spread loads on thin materials.",
    "The self-drilling screws and roll pins fit my ongoing mechanical repair work, with roll pins adding a fastening option beyond my existing cotter pins.",
    "Rubber grommets and small single-use glue tubes support practical repair tasks: protecting wires through drilled holes and making occasional bonds alongside my epoxy and tapes."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Calibration weights do not follow from my caliper purchase: measuring dimensions does not mean I have a small scale that needs calibration.",
    "Long exterior deck screws and six rolls of plumbing tape assume specific projects I have not shown a current need for.",
    "Push-on retainers and wire connectors are relevant to repair work, but I would wait for a job requiring their particular sizes or connections before choosing them."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in workshop supplies seems to have been stretched into an assumed need for plumbing, exterior woodwork, and scale calibration supplies.",
    "My repeated purchases of assortments seem to be treated as a reason to recommend more assortments, even when their contents do not solve a current need."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Supplies that complement my existing bolts, rivets, and repair tools matter more to me than items that merely share a broad home-repair purpose.",
    "Exact dimensions and intended use matter: grommets need to fit my holes, retainers need to fit the parts, and long deck screws are not interchangeable with general mechanical fasteners.",
    "Already owning self-tapping screws makes another set less urgent, while washers fill a useful supporting role alongside my bolt assortments."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognize my practical fastening and repair interests but sometimes mistake a related workshop use for a current project need."
}
